title: 2004 AMC 10A Problem 18
statement: A sequence of three real numbers forms an arithmetic progression with a first term of \(9.\) If \(2\) is added to the second term and \(20\) is added to the third term, the three resulting numbers form a geometric progression. What is the smallest possible value for the third term of the geometric progression?

solutions.text:
The arithmetic progression is \(9,\) \(9 + d,\) \(9 + 2d,\) so the geometric progression is \(9,\) \(11 + d,\) \(29 + 2d.\)

The geometric condition gives \[ (11 + d)^2 = 9(29 + 2d), \] which simplifies to \(d^2 + 4d - 140 = 0,\) so \(d = 10\) or \(d = -14.\)

The third terms \(29 + 2d\) are \(49\) and \(1.\) The smallest is \(1.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Write the progression as \(9,\) \(9 + d,\) \(9 + 2d,\) so the geometric one is \(9,\) \(11 + d,\) \(29 + 2d\)
Use \((11 + d)^2 = 9(29 + 2d)\) and take the value of \(d\) giving the smaller third term
